description.from:
**Milestone:** M1, first slice

**Goal.** As the service, I turn one accepted event into one queued delivery per person and channel. First version: operator kinds go to the operators in SSM; preferences arrive in S_PREFS.

**Build.**
- `src/caducus/notify/routing.py`, `src/caducus/notify/handlers/router.py`, SQS `caducus-ingest` with a dead-letter queue, consumer with SQS maximum concurrency (not reserved concurrency: other accounts here have a Lambda concurrency limit of only 10, see `infra/monitoring/papyrus-monitoring.yaml` for the workaround).
- Conditional put on `EVENT#<eventId>` / `META` for dedupe. Per-channel SQS queues; `src/caducus/notify/channels/base.py` defines `Channel.send(delivery) -> Outcome`, so Slack, Discord and a later generic webhook are added without touching routing.

**Acceptance.**
Unit and behave tests; a redelivered SQS message makes no second delivery.

**Depends on:** kanbus-6eb0c5, kanbus-53a88d

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: Routing
  Scenario: An operator event reaches each operator once
    Given two operators are configured
    When an operator event arrives twice
    Then each operator has exactly one queued email delivery

  Scenario: A kind with no audience is visible
    Given no operators are configured
    When an operator event arrives
    Then the delivery log records "refused" with the reason "no audience"
```
